title: A Royal Shield for Ruy Lopez
body: In the sixteenth century, a Spanish priest named Ruy Lopez wrote an important book about chess. To protect his hard work, King Philip the Second granted him a special ten-year monopoly. Back then, book laws were so strict that anyone who copied a book without permission could face massive fines or even the death penalty!

variants.lucy: Long ago in Spain, a gentle priest named Ruy Lopez spent many quiet hours writing down his favorite chess secrets in a special book. To keep this treasure safe, the king himself promised that no one else could print the book for ten whole years. It was like a royal shield made of paper and ink, protecting the priest's hard work.
variants.luca: But watch out, because copying that book without permission was an incredibly dangerous move back then! King Philip the Second set up rules so fierce that thieves faced giant fines or even the ultimate punishment. It was a high-stakes adventure just to guard those chess pages from rivals.
variants.cn: 很久以前的西班牙，有一位温和的神父，名叫鲁伊·洛佩斯。他花了许许多多安静的时光，把自己最喜欢的国际象棋秘密写进一本特别的书里。为了保护这件宝贝，国王亲自许下承诺：整整十年里，谁也不许印这本书。这就像一面用纸和墨水做成的皇家盾牌，守护着神父辛勤的成果。

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath

titleCn: 鲁伊·洛佩斯的皇家盾牌
